findings.conditions: SC_NOTIFY_SUPERSET called twice in a row on the same communicator; one receiver is slow to enter or finish its probe loop while a sender has already finished call k and posted its call k+1 TRUE (or EXTRA) message
findings.reasoning: The superset algorithm has no synchronisation between calls. It counts down num_super_senders using Iprobe(ANY_SOURCE) on two tags, SUPER_TRUE and SUPER_EXTRA. A fast sender can finish call k and Isend its call k+1 message while this rank is still polling in call k. Messages with different tags are not ordered against each other, so a k+1 TRUE message can be matched before the same sender's pending call-k EXTRA message. Even with equal tags, once the k message has been consumed the k+1 one matches the wildcard probe. The bsearch assert passes because the source is a valid super sender. The rank then records a wrong sender or payload, or counts one sender twice, and the leftover message is consumed in the next call. The result is wrong sender lists or payloads in both calls.

findings.conditions: Back-to-back sc_notify_payload calls of type NBX on the same comm; a fast rank sees its Ibarrier complete and Issends the next call's NBX message before a slower rank's MPI_Test observes barrier completion
findings.reasoning: Each NBX loop iteration calls Iprobe(ANY_SOURCE, SC_TAG_NOTIFY_NBX) before MPI_Test on the Ibarrier. The barrier may already be complete globally while this rank has not yet observed it. Meanwhile a rank that has observed it returns and starts the next notify, issuing new Issends with the same tag. The slow rank's Iprobe can match such a message and receive it into the current call. That adds a spurious sender and payload here. The Issend completes, so the next call silently loses that sender. Each call's tag and communicator are identical, so nothing separates the rounds.

findings.conditions: sc_notify_payloadv with type NBX and sorted == 0, and at least one rank having receivers
findings.reasoning: sc_notify_payloadv_nbx sends with MPI_Issend tag SC_TAG_NOTIFY_NBXV (line 2058), but it probes and receives only SC_TAG_NOTIFY_NBX (lines 2087/2106). The payload messages are never matched, so the synchronous sends never complete and Testall never succeeds. No rank with receivers ever enters the Ibarrier, and every rank spins forever. The wildcard probe can also match NBX-tagged messages from a concurrent or next sc_notify_payload NBX call by another rank. Those would be received with the wrong layout and counts. The tests only exercise the sorted path, which goes through the wrapper, so this path is untested.

findings.conditions: Consecutive NARY notify calls on the same comm; one level-L message to rank B is delayed while a peer A finishes the call and sends its next-call message with the same level tag to B
findings.reasoning: In sc_notify_recursive_nary, rank B receives nrecv messages per level through Probe(ANY_SOURCE, NARY+level). It derives the slot j from the source and does not check whether that slot was already filled. Peer A delivers its items for B at this level and needs nothing more from B to finish the call. Its Isends may complete eagerly, and with depth 1 the first thing the next call does is send to B again with the same tag. If the message from a third peer C is still in flight, B can match A's new message. B then overwrites A's slot with next-call data, leaking the old buffer, and leaves C's message for the next call. The merged results in both calls are wrong.
